models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Near-calm tonight at Panarea - 3 kt SE, gusts 6, swell 0.1 ft; light SE filling in to around 9 kt tomorrow.
briefing.synopsis: The payload carries no pressure analysis, so take this as a wind-field read rather than a chart: today's flow around the islands has been light and directionally unstable, NNW-NW through the middle of the day and backing N to NE this evening (Panarea 4.3 kt from 322° at 18:00, ECMWF/ICON consensus). Overnight the wind backs into the SE quadrant across the whole group and slowly fills - Panarea 3.1 kt from 110° at midnight, 4.2 kt SSE at 06:00, then 7.0 kt at midday and 8.2 kt ESE by 18:00 Tuesday. By Wednesday 00:00 it peaks near 8.7 kt SSE gusting 17.5 kt at Panarea before easing again at dawn. Nothing in the next 48 h exceeds Force 3 at any of the fleet's islands.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: San Pietro buoy field is the recommendation and the choice genuinely does not matter tonight - all three Panarea options score within 0.001 of each other (San Pietro 0.941, Drautto and Cala Zimmari 0.940). ECMWF IFS 06Z / ICON-2i 12Z consensus gives 3.2 kt SE, gusts 6.2 kt, swell 0.1 ft from the NNW: San Pietro's exposed arc is 30-180° so the breeze is nominally on the nose of the field, but at 3 kt it is academic. The thing that would move the fleet is the SE filling earlier than modelled - if it is already over 10 kt from the SSE before midnight, Cala Zimmari / Milazzese is the tighter arc (80-190°) and worth the shift; otherwise stay put.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: Tuesday morning stays light at Panarea - around 4.2 kt SSE, gusts 6.4 kt at 06:00, building to about 7 kt by midday and 8.2 kt ESE by evening. For any boats that ran up to Stromboli, the optional return to Panarea (11 nm, 219°T) is forecast go in every window from 06:00 to 14:00, with 4.5 kt SE gusting 6.8 at the 06:00 start and 7.3 kt gusting 13.6 by midday; waves 0.3 ft throughout. Recommended departure 06:00 for the flattest water and a beam reach either way - expect to motor-sail in under 7 kt.

passage_notes.note: Go in all windows. 4.5 kt SE gusting 6.8 at 06:00 rising to 7.3 kt gusting 13.6 by midday, waves 0.3 ft, beam reach at TWA 80-93°. Recommended start 06:00. Note Marina del Gabbiano is open from every direction and no anchoring - shelter there depends entirely on it staying calm.

Go in all windows but a light-air motor-sail: 4.8-6.0 kt S to ESE, waves 0.9-1.0 ft, broad reach to run. Gusts of 15-19 kt appear against 5-6 kt means - these are interval-maximum values from a single model in light air, reported not treated as a caution. 06:00 start recommended for the 28 nm.
Go, but the breeze is on the nose: 3.1-5.2 kt SE/ESE with TWA 14-40°, i.e. head to wind in most windows. Waves 0.7-0.8 ft. Plan to motor; 06:00 departure gives the only close-hauled angle of the day.

Recommended departure 07:00. The 06:00 window is flagged no-go on thunderstorms in the passage window. From 08:00 it is go: 12.2 kt WNW broad reach early, easing to 5-7 kt WSW in the afternoon with waves building 1.0 ft to 2.3 ft. This is four days out - treat it as a trend.

cautions: Tuesday night at Panarea the SSE fills to about 9 kt gusting 17.5 kt (San Pietro) and blows straight into the exposed arc of all three buoy fields, with 0.5 ft ESE swell - fine numbers, but expect a rolly night and check bridles.

The 06:00 Salina → Portorosa window on 9 Oct is a computed no-go for forecast thunderstorms; 07:00 is the recommended start. That is a conservative threshold, not a decision - review it closer to the day.

Models disagree by more than 6 kt at several hours from Tuesday night onward: Lipari 00:00 Wed spans 1.9-10.2 kt, Filicudi 18:00 Wed spans 0.6-10.8 kt, Salina 18:00 Wed 1.8-11.5 kt. Quote those as ranges, not the means.
